title: Add fleet TmuxBackend for waves and move the screen classifier into fleet
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p fleet && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee herding::
action: Per D4, ONE classifier. Step 1 — move: create `crates/fleet/src/screen.rs` (declare `pub mod screen;` in fleet's lib.rs) holding `pub struct ScreenSettings { pub busy_markers: Vec<String>, pub blocked_markers: Vec<String>, pub scrollback: u32, pub quiet_cycles: u32, pub interval_ms: u64 }` with the SAME defaults bee's `TmuxSettings::default()` carries today (read `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/tmux.rs` — copy the literals, do not re-derive), `pub enum Screen { Idle, Working, Blocked }`, and `pub fn classify(screen: &str, s: &ScreenSettings) -> Screen` with the exact semantics bee's `classify` has (blocked wins, last-12/last-2 non-empty-line windows, case-insensitive). Move bee's classifier tests into fleet beside it. Then make bee's tmux.rs REUSE it: `TmuxSettings` becomes a thin alias/newtype over `fleet::screen::ScreenSettings` (keep `TmuxSettings::from_config(cfg)` in bee — config parsing is bee's), and bee's `classify` calls `fleet::screen::classify`; delete the duplicate body. bee's tmux tests must stay green unchanged apart from the import. Step 2 — backend: create `crates/fleet/src/backend/tmux.rs` with `pub struct TmuxBackend` implementing `WorkerBackend` as a peer of `HerdrBackend` (declare `pub mod tmux;` in backend.rs beside `pub mod herdr;`), with `new(agent_kind, agent_args, settings: ScreenSettings)` and `with_test_seams(dirs, spill_dir, …)` mirroring herdr.rs (reuse the `child_path` PATH-PREPEND idea — prepend, never replace; the stub script needs coreutils). Worker names are tmux pane ids (`%N`) or pane titles: `canonical_id(name)` → if `%N`-shaped return it, else `tmux display-message -p -t <name> '#{pane_id}'`, on failure return the name unchanged (no-collapse default); `start(spec)` → type one shell-quoted `exec '<kind>' '<args>…'` line into the pane via `send-keys -t <pane> -l <line>` + separate `send-keys -t <pane> Enter` (never -p/--print); `status(name)` → `capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -<scrollback>` then `classify`: Idle → `WorkerStatus::Ready`, Working → `Working`, Blocked → `Blocked`, any failure → `Unverifiable` (never Err); `send(name, task)` → wrap the task with the same spill-file instruction herdr.rs uses (`wrap_task_with_spill_instruction` — make it `pub(crate)` shared or copy with a pointer), then the two-call send, and refuse with Err when the pre-send capture classifies Blocked (tmux-herding-transport D3); `read_output(name)` → capture-pane plus `recover_transcript` from the spill file (reuse herdr.rs's helper the same way). Step 3 — selection: in bee's wave.rs, `fn real_backend_ctor(kind: String, args: Vec<String>) -> HerdrBackend` (anchor `rg -n "fn real_backend_ctor" …/wave.rs`) is passed by `wave()` as `construct_backend`; make the production path pick by `transport_kind_at(main_root)`: keep `real_backend_ctor` byte-identical for Herdr and add a NAMED constructor factory `fn tmux_backend_ctor(settings: ScreenSettings) -> impl FnOnce(String, Vec<String>) -> TmuxBackend`; the call site passes `tmux_backend_ctor(settings)` by name, never an inline closure literal — this honors the doctrine in the comment above `real_backend_ctor` (wave.rs ~572-582) because a test can call `tmux_backend_ctor(settings)(kind, args)` directly and assert on what it built. `settings` comes from bee's `TmuxSettings::from_config(&cfg)` converted into `ScreenSettings`. `build_wave_backend_and_run` is generic over `B`, so dispatch with a `match transport_kind_at(main_root)` that calls it once per concrete type (both arms return the same Result type) — do not box. Also widen bee tmux.rs's test seam `with_test_path` to `pub(crate)` (it is private today) so sibling modules' tests can reuse it later. Tests: `crates/fleet/tests/tmux_backend.rs` with a PATH-prepended stub `tmux` (mirror `herdr_backend.rs`'s `Stub`): start types two send-keys calls with `-l` and a separate Enter; status maps the three screens to Ready/Working/Blocked and a failing stub to Unverifiable; send refuses on a blocked screen; canonical_id passes `%3` through and resolves a title via display-message; read_output recovers a spill. In bee: a test that `wave` under transport=tmux constructs the tmux ctor (assert through a seam the way `real_backend_ctor_hands_kind_and_args_straight_through_to_construction` does). Test in bee (name prefixed `wave_tmux_`): `tmux_backend_ctor(settings)(kind, args)` hands kind/args/settings straight through, mirroring `real_backend_ctor_hands_kind_and_args_straight_through_to_construction`.
